ANU Exploration Robotics EXR Exploration Robotics ANU Student Club Home About Team The people behind the build Mission What we are building and why Partners Organisations supporting us — per aspera ad profunda Mission Exploring and surveying the world around us with custom-made autonomous robots. 2026 / 2027 Who we are What the club does ANU Exploration Robotics is a student-run club operating in Canberra.
Our focus is on the exploration and surveying of the world around us through the use of custom-made, autonomous robots.
To accommodate this goal, we enter competitions on the world stage, allowing us and our robots to gain experience that can be used on sustainable initiatives.
Membership is open to students of any year level and any discipline, and no prior robotics experience is required.
Mission objectives Initial goals To make a submarine for the RobotX RoboSub competition, and complete as many tasks in the competition as possible.
RoboSub RoboSub is an international student competition run by RoboNation and held annually in the United States.
Teams build autonomous underwater vehicles that complete a course of tasks with no operator input and no tether once the vehicle is released.
Tasks include navigating gates, identifying and localising objects by computer vision, homing on acoustic pingers, and releasing markers.
Teams are also assessed on a technical design report and a design presentation.
Prototype 1.0 Prototype 1.0 is a tethered underwater vehicle controlled by an operator from an offboard computer.
It is the foundation for a competition vehicle rather than an entry in itself, and is required to meet the following.
ID Requirement Verification R-01 Have a waterproof housing rated for depths of up to 2.1 metres, which is 20.6 kPa.
Test R-02 Achieve controlled surge, heave through buoyancy control, and yaw movement.
Demonstration R-03 Be neutrally buoyant to within 0.5 percent of its mass when shut off.
Test R-04 Maintain predictable underwater handling.
Demonstration R-05 Be controlled by an operator from an offboard computer through a tethered communications link.
Demonstration R-06 Include a clear and accessible kill switch at the stern.
Propulsion must not turn back on when the kill switch is deactivated after use.
Test R-07 Passively maintain stable roll and pitch during normal operation.
Analysis and test R-08 Be battery operated.
Inspection R-09 Have variable propulsion control to adjust the acceleration and velocity of the vehicle.
Demonstration R-10 Allow major components to be accessed or replaced without requiring redesign.
Inspection R-11 Provide sufficient provisions for the future integration of upgrades and competition specific mechanisms.

Inspection Looking ahead Future directions Although our current goals align with submarine development for the RobotX RoboSub competition, in the future we are looking forward to expanding our design principles into other design projects and different vehicles.
These future projects would include: Marine reef and wildlife conservation We hope to explore the use of robotics to observe and map ocean wildlife.
Robotics of this kind can have a tremendous impact on the conservation of coral reef systems and wildlife populations through monitoring and scanning them.

The UAV Challenge: Outback Rescue An Australian competition in which an autonomous aircraft must locate a stranded person, represented by a mannequin known as Outback Joe, and complete a retrieval or delivery task.
Entering would take the club beyond underwater vehicles into aerial systems, drawing on the same work in autonomy, perception and vehicle design.
Depth project An attempt at a depth record for a vehicle designed and built entirely by undergraduates.

The engineering sits in pressure housing design, seal and penetrator selection, and structural analysis at depths far beyond anything a pool can be used to test, which makes analysis and proof testing the whole of the problem.
Support Supporting the club The club is funded through member contributions and external support.
Sponsorship goes toward parts, fabrication and testing for the build.
Support in kind is as useful to us as cash.
Components, machining or fabrication time, workshop access and technical mentoring all contribute directly to the build.

Milestone 25 August 2026 Prototype 1.0 project brief approved The project brief for Prototype 1.0 was approved, setting eleven requirements (R-01 to R-11), each with its own verification method.
It defines the vehicle as a tethered proof of concept for controlled surge, heave, and yaw, and commits the team to the V model, with four formal reviews between requirements and pool trials.
